content.comment_body: Hello everyone, With the [product_name] [article_no], is it correct that you can store up to 2000 records on an SD card? 1. Is it possible to increase this limit beyond 2000 records? 2. What happens when the storage limit is reached—does it start overwriting old records? Thanks for your help.

Hello, The maximum number of entries is 2000. Once that is reached, the oldest records are replaced (FIFO method). If you switch the device to Stop mode, it will create an extra datalog on the SD card. You can copy the old files to your PC by inserting the SD card and transferring the files. Hope this clarifies things. Also, to record onto the SD card, you must switch the [product_name] to Stop mode before uploading, then back to Run mode. After doing this, you'll get an additional datalog file on the SD card.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exchanging information about the data logging limitations of the [product_name] [article_no] with SD card use, particularly focusing on the storage capacity and system behavior when the maximum record count is reached. There are questions regarding data expanding capabilities and uncertainty about the overwrite method once the 2000-record limit is met. The device uses a FIFO system that replaces older entries when full, and operational steps such as switching modes play a role in managing and retrieving data files.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the potential to store more than 2000 records and want confirmation of how the device handles files when capacity is reached, such as automatic overwriting. They seek simple data management and request clear instructions for extracting recorded files.
